context: Attribute names with labels, levels, role, category, description, causal mechanism, and directional dependency hints (known upstream drivers and downstream effects) — structured to support causal discovery without fully specifying the DAG.

variables.name: GoodStudent
variables.label: Good student status
variables.description: Whether the driver qualifies as a good student via GPA thresholds.
variables.mechanism: GoodStudent is jointly determined by Age (students are predominantly Adolescent or young Adult) and SocioEcon (academic performance correlates with socio-economic resources). It is used as a risk proxy that feeds RiskAversion: good students tend to be more cautious drivers. It has no direct effect on vehicle or cost nodes.

variables.name: Age
variables.label: Driver age group
variables.description: Driver's age bracket; primary demographic risk factor.
variables.mechanism: Root node with no modeled parents. Age directly shapes multiple downstream attributes: it influences GoodStudent eligibility (Adolescent most likely), SeniorTrain availability (Senior only), and DrivingSkill (Adolescent and Senior have elevated SubStandard probability). It is the most broadly connected demographic root node.

variables.name: SocioEcon
variables.label: Socio-economic status
variables.description: Household socio-economic tier; shapes vehicle and neighbourhood choices.
variables.mechanism: Root node. SocioEcon determines the type of vehicle a driver can afford (MakeModel), the neighbourhood they live in (HomeBase), and influences GoodStudent status. Wealthier drivers tend toward Luxury/SuperLuxury vehicles and Secure/Suburb neighbourhoods; lower SocioEcon toward Economy vehicles and City/Rural areas.

variables.name: RiskAversion
variables.label: Risk aversion tendency
variables.description: Dispositional attitude toward risk; shapes driving behaviour.
variables.mechanism: RiskAversion is influenced by GoodStudent (good students trend Cautious/Normal) and is itself a direct input to DrivQuality. Lower risk aversion (Psychopath, Adventurous) produces Poor driving quality independently of skill level. It also influences Mileage: risk-seeking drivers tend to drive more.

variables.name: VehicleYear
variables.label: Vehicle model year
variables.description: Model year recency; proxy for safety feature availability.
variables.mechanism: Root node. VehicleYear is a key determinant of whether modern safety technologies are present: Current vehicles have much higher probability of Antilock brakes and Airbags than older vehicles. It also contributes to CarValue (newer = higher value) along with MakeModel.

variables.name: ThisCarDam
variables.label: Damage to insured car
variables.description: Physical damage severity to the insured vehicle.
variables.mechanism: ThisCarDam is jointly determined by Accident severity and RuggedAuto (structural protection): a severe accident in an EggShell vehicle produces maximum damage, while the same accident in a Tank produces less. ThisCarDam directly drives ThisCarCost (the repair/replacement bill for the insured car).

variables.name: RuggedAuto
variables.label: Vehicle structural ruggedness
variables.description: Structural crashworthiness; modulates damage from a given accident.
variables.mechanism: RuggedAuto is determined by MakeModel: economy/sports cars tend toward EggShell; family sedans toward Football; large luxury/SUV types toward Tank. It acts as a damage moderator between Accident severity and ThisCarDam, and also jointly determines Cushioning (with Airbag).

variables.name: Accident
variables.label: Accident severity
variables.description: Overall accident severity; the central loss event in the network.
variables.mechanism: Accident is the central outcome node of the driving sub-network. It is determined by DrivQuality (primary driver of at-fault severity), Mileage (exposure — more miles = more opportunities for accidents), Antilock (safety system that reduces severity), and OtherCar (presence of another vehicle amplifies severity). Accident then feeds both vehicle damage (ThisCarDam, OtherCarCost) and injury costs (MedCost).

variables.name: MakeModel
variables.label: Car make/model class
variables.description: Vehicle category; determines vehicle attributes and value.
variables.mechanism: MakeModel is determined by SocioEcon (wealth drives vehicle tier). It is the primary vehicle-side root that cascades into RuggedAuto (structural class), CarValue (market value), and availability of safety features (Antilock, Airbag) through VehicleYear interactions.

variables.name: DrivQuality
variables.label: Driving quality
variables.description: Synthesized overall driving performance.
variables.mechanism: DrivQuality is jointly produced by DrivingSkill (technical competency) and RiskAversion (behavioural disposition). A highly skilled but reckless driver (Expert + Psychopath) produces Normal quality at best; a cautious but sub-standard driver produces Poor quality. DrivQuality is the primary proximate cause of Accident severity.

variables.name: Mileage
variables.label: Annual mileage bucket
variables.description: Annual miles driven; pure exposure variable.
variables.mechanism: Mileage is influenced by RiskAversion (risk-seeking drivers accumulate more miles) and is a pure exposure multiplier: holding DrivQuality constant, higher mileage proportionally raises the probability of experiencing an Accident. Domino represents extreme/commercial-level mileage.

variables.name: Antilock
variables.label: Antilock braking system (ABS)
variables.description: ABS presence; reduces accident severity probability.
variables.mechanism: Antilock availability is determined by both MakeModel (standard on Luxury/SuperLuxury; optional on others) and VehicleYear (Current vehicles much more likely to have ABS). ABS directly reduces the probability of severe Accident outcomes by preventing wheel lock-up.

variables.name: DrivingSkill
variables.label: Driver skill level
variables.description: Technical driving competency; shaped by experience and training.
variables.mechanism: DrivingSkill is determined by Age (Adolescents lack experience → SubStandard more likely; Seniors may decline → higher SubStandard probability), SeniorTrain (completed training improves Senior skill), and DrivHist (more prior incidents → lower skill rating). It feeds DrivQuality as the technical component.

variables.name: SeniorTrain
variables.label: Senior driver training
variables.description: Completion of senior driver refresher program.
variables.mechanism: SeniorTrain is available only to Senior-age drivers (Age=Senior → non-trivial probability of True; other ages → near-zero). When True, it improves DrivingSkill. It is a targeted intervention node whose effect is conditional on Age.

variables.name: ThisCarCost
variables.label: Insured car claim cost
variables.description: Financial cost to repair/replace the insured vehicle.
variables.mechanism: ThisCarCost is determined by ThisCarDam (severity of damage to the insured car) and CarValue (replacement cost basis). Severe damage to a high-value car drives costs to HundredThou or Million; mild damage to a low-value car stays at Thousand. ThisCarCost feeds the aggregate PropCost comparison node.

variables.name: Theft
variables.label: Vehicle theft
variables.description: Whether the insured vehicle was stolen.
variables.mechanism: Theft probability is determined by CarValue (high-value cars are more attractive targets), HomeBase (City neighbourhoods have higher theft rates than Secure/Rural), and AntiTheft (deterrence system directly reduces theft probability). Theft generates a total-loss cost that feeds ThisCarCost.

variables.name: CarValue
variables.label: Insured car value
variables.description: Market value of the insured car; determines theft attractiveness and repair cost ceiling.
variables.mechanism: CarValue is determined by MakeModel (Luxury/SuperLuxury → higher value) and VehicleYear (Current → higher value). CarValue drives both Theft probability (valuable cars more targeted) and ThisCarCost (replacement cost ceiling).

variables.name: HomeBase
variables.label: Home neighbourhood type
variables.description: Neighbourhood type; modulates theft and ambient risk exposure.
variables.mechanism: HomeBase is determined by SocioEcon (Wealthy → Secure/Suburb; lower → City). It directly influences Theft probability (City has highest crime rates) and OtherCar probability (City driving involves more traffic density).

variables.name: AntiTheft
variables.label: Anti-theft system
variables.description: Presence of anti-theft device; primary theft deterrent.
variables.mechanism: AntiTheft is more likely on Luxury/SuperLuxury vehicles (MakeModel) and Current vehicles (VehicleYear). When present, it directly and substantially reduces Theft probability. It has no effect on accident severity or other non-theft outcomes.

variables.name: PropCost
variables.label: Proportional cost comparison
variables.description: Relative cost bucket comparing this-car to other-car costs.
variables.mechanism: PropCost aggregates ThisCarCost and OtherCarCost into a comparative summary used for policy pricing and claim prioritization. It is a terminal aggregation node with no downstream effects in the model.

variables.name: OtherCarCost
variables.label: Other car claim cost
variables.description: Third-party vehicle repair/replacement cost.
variables.mechanism: OtherCarCost is driven by Accident severity and whether another vehicle is involved (OtherCar=True is a prerequisite for non-trivial OtherCarCost). Severe accidents with another car produce the highest third-party costs. It feeds PropCost.

variables.name: OtherCar
variables.label: Other vehicle involved
variables.description: Whether a second vehicle participates in the incident.
variables.mechanism: OtherCar probability is influenced by HomeBase (higher traffic density in City increases multi-vehicle collision likelihood) and Mileage (more exposure). OtherCar=True amplifies Accident severity (multi-vehicle crashes are more severe on average) and is the prerequisite for OtherCarCost.

variables.name: MedCost
variables.label: Medical treatment cost
variables.description: Medical cost of injuries from the accident.
variables.mechanism: MedCost is determined by Accident severity and Cushioning quality. Severe accidents with Poor cushioning generate Million-level medical costs; mild accidents with Excellent cushioning stay at Thousand. MedCost feeds ILiCost (injury+liability aggregate).

variables.name: Cushioning
variables.label: Occupant cushioning quality
variables.description: Integrated occupant protection quality; determines injury severity given an accident.
variables.mechanism: Cushioning is determined by Airbag (primary active safety input) and RuggedAuto (structural passive protection). Airbag=True + RuggedAuto=Tank → Excellent cushioning; Airbag=False + RuggedAuto=EggShell → Poor. Cushioning modulates how accident severity translates into MedCost.

variables.name: Airbag
variables.label: Airbag present
variables.description: Airbag availability; primary active occupant protection.
variables.mechanism: Airbag presence is determined by MakeModel (standard on Luxury/SuperLuxury; rare on Economy) and VehicleYear (Current vehicles standard-equipped). Airbag is the dominant input to Cushioning quality; its presence reduces injury severity (MedCost) through improved Cushioning.

variables.name: ILiCost
variables.label: Injury / liability cost
variables.description: Aggregated injury and legal liability cost bucket.
variables.mechanism: ILiCost aggregates medical costs (MedCost) into a total injury-and-liability cost bucket, incorporating third-party liability exposure. It is a terminal cost-aggregation leaf node with no downstream effects in the model.

variables.name: DrivHist
variables.label: Prior driving incidents
variables.description: Bucketed count of prior at-fault incidents or violations.
variables.mechanism: Root node. DrivHist is a historical record of driving incidents that directly informs DrivingSkill assessment: Many incidents → SubStandard skill more probable. It is also used directly in actuarial rating models. DrivHist is causally upstream of DrivingSkill and has no other modeled parents.
